spec.title: Zap project pause, stop and continuation

status.comment: Owner addition of 2026-09-15. Per-project lifecycle controls are included in the active workspace implementation; state is observed, not inferred from a button click.

p.project-lifecycle: Zap Wayfinder exposes separately authorized Pause, Stop and Continue actions for an exact project/work context. Project execution state is distinct from coordinator/worker process state and from semantic plan completion. Action requests, pending transitions and observed settled states have durable identities and revisions; all clients observe the committed project state.

p.pause: Pause first prevents new dispatch for the project and retains its queued work and user input. It requests supported interruption or a safe stopping point for active owned coordinator/worker turns. The project remains pausing until the relevant observations establish that work has settled; unsupported or unknown control is explicit. No adapter claims to freeze an arbitrary in-flight LLM computation and later resume the same computation at the same token. Viewing activity, output and history remains available.

p.stop: Stop prevents new execution, records cancellation/retention decisions for queued attempts and requests termination of the project's owned active work and resources. It preserves the plan, source/attempt basis, chat, question/answer history, outputs and available results. Process exit does not mean a task was accepted. Stop is not project deletion or repository rollback, and control of unrelated user-started processes is not inferred from an observed session identifier.

p.continue: Continue restores the registered project context and resumable coordinator conversation. Before new planned mutations it checks current source/plan state and reconciles uncertain prior outcomes. Paused pending input is delivered through the same scoped dispatch mechanism; stopped/cancelled attempts may become new attempts with preserved lineage rather than blind command replay. A changed policy or UI focus does not itself recreate the expensive coordinator boot. Lost native context or unavailable resume is an explicit recovery state.

p.project-isolation: Pausing or stopping one project must not stop another project sharing the same model profile or account. Shared host processes are permitted only where verified project/session-scoped control provides this isolation. If only process-wide termination can enforce ownership, use separate project/context-owned host processes. Interruptions, process handles, descendant scope and incarnation epochs are validated before control; no generic kill-by-process-name operation implements a project action.

p.paused-input: While paused or stopped, user messages, new specification signals and ordinary answers can be retained as input without silently restarting execution. An answer to a now-resolved native permission request does not authorize a later unrelated request. The UI distinguishes saved input, pending delivery and actual continuation. Explicit user Continue, with applicable scope and current policy, re-enables dispatch.

p.verification: A bounded two-project proof verifies that pause/stop of A leaves B running and observable, repeat requests do not duplicate actions, retained history survives, and continuation reuses known session state without another bootstrap where supported. Fake host processes cover ownership/control semantics; a short inexpensive Codex probe establishes only the actual supported native path. No cross-provider matrix or destructive real-project test is required.
